summary: Jimma Airport (JIM/HAJM) is a regional airport serving the city of Jimma in southwestern Ethiopia, historically the capital of the Kingdom of Jimma and today the administrative center of the Jimma Zone. Situated at an elevation of around 5,500 feet, it primarily handles domestic flights linking the highland city to Addis Ababa and supporting travel to one of Ethiopia's most important coffee-producing regions.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate at Jimma Airport?
A: Ethiopian Airlines is the primary carrier operating scheduled domestic flights between Jimma and Addis Ababa Bole International Airport.

Q: How far is Jimma Airport from the city center?
A: The airport is located a short drive of roughly 5 to 10 kilometers from central Jimma, depending on traffic and route taken.

Q: Is Jimma Airport domestic or international?
A: Jimma Airport is a domestic airport handling only scheduled internal flights within Ethiopia, with no current international service.

Q: What is the elevation of Jimma Airport?
A: The airport sits at approximately 5,500 feet (1,675 meters) above sea level in the Ethiopian highlands.
transport_tips: Taxis and bajaj (three-wheeled auto-rickshaws) are commonly available outside the terminal and offer affordable transfers to Jimma town center. Pre-arranging a hotel pickup is recommended during early morning or late evening flights since ride options can be limited at those hours. The road from the airport to the city is generally in fair condition but can slow down during the rainy season.
local_tip: If you have a layover or extra time in Jimma, ask locals to direct you to a nearby coffee ceremony (buna) — the Jimma zone is one of the original growing regions for Arabica coffee and the freshly roasted local brew is a highlight of any visit.
